lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Independent application: building a fallback before committing

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic building a fallback before committing task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner reads a provided fictional scenario in which a character is relying entirely on one teacher to submit a single recommendation letter for a scholarship application with a fixed deadline, with no backup plan if it doesn't come through in time, and builds a concrete fallback with a specific switch-over trigger before the deadline arrives.
safetyNotes: The scenario is fictional and does not require the learner to name or rely on any real teacher, deadline, or application of their own.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l05-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l05-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l05-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l05-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Why is deciding the trigger condition in advance different from just deciding 'I'll switch to Plan B if things don't work out'? What could go wrong without a specific trigger?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u05-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Risk identification: At least three specific risks are listed using scenario details. | Fallback specificity: Fallback names a specific, workable alternative. | Trigger condition quality: Trigger names a specific date or event tied to the deadline. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner identify a point at which even Plan B could fail, and sketch in one or two sentences what the character's next move would be if that happened too.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic building a fallback before committing task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: paper or notes app
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: building a fallback before committing worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner reads a provided fictional scenario in which a character is relying entirely on one teacher to submit a single recommendation letter for a scholarship application with a fixed deadline, with no backup plan if it doesn't come through in time, and builds a concrete fallback with a specific switch-over trigger before the deadline arrives.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact building a fallback before committing decision or action.
Model move 2: Before building a fallback, state Plan A and why the character currently believes it is enough.
Model move 3: List at least three specific things that could cause Plan A to fail, using the details given in the scenario.

Model check: Risk identification: At least three specific risks are listed using scenario details. | Fallback specificity: Fallback names a specific, workable alternative. | Trigger condition quality: Trigger names a specific date or event tied to the deadline.

resources.title: building a fallback before committing action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for building a fallback before committing.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: building a fallback before committing coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner reads a provided fictional scenario in which a character is relying entirely on one teacher to submit a single recommendation letter for a scholarship application with a fixed deadline, with no backup plan if it doesn't come through in time, and builds a concrete fallback with a specific switch-over trigger before the deadline arrives.
Coach direction: Before building a fallback, state Plan A and why the character currently believes it is enough.
Learner prompt: What is the character's Plan A, and why does the character currently believe no backup is needed?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: building a fallback before committing complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: List at least three specific things that could cause Plan A to fail, using the details given in the scenario.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I listed at least three specific ways Plan A could fail (not just 'it might not work').
Response 2 (t2-p2): At least one of my listed risks is something the character could notice before the deadline itself, not only on the deadline.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: building a fallback before committing minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Why is deciding the trigger condition in advance different from just deciding 'I'll switch to Plan B if things don't work out'? What could go wrong without a specific trigger?

Success checks: Risk identification: At least three specific risks are listed using scenario details. | Fallback specificity: Fallback names a specific, workable alternative. | Trigger condition quality: Trigger names a specific date or event tied to the deadline.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: building a fallback before committing supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l05-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g11-u05-l05-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional building a fallback before committing condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Risk identification: At least three specific risks are listed using scenario details. | Fallback specificity: Fallback names a specific, workable alternative. | Trigger condition quality: Trigger names a specific date or event tied to the deadline..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l05-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guidedFirstAttempt.setup: The learner reads a provided fictional scenario in which a character is relying entirely on one teacher to submit a single recommendation letter for a scholarship application with a fixed deadline, with no backup plan if it doesn't come through in time, and builds a concrete fallback with a specific switch-over trigger before the deadline arrives.

simulationRoute.title: building a fallback before committing — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the building a fallback before committing task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Why is deciding the trigger condition in advance different from just deciding 'I'll switch to Plan B if things don't work out'? What could go wrong without a specific trigger?
observableCriteria: Risk identification: At least three specific risks are listed using scenario details.
Fallback specificity: Fallback names a specific, workable alternative.
Trigger condition quality: Trigger names a specific date or event tied to the deadline.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u05-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Risk identification: At least three specific risks are listed using scenario details. | Fallback specificity: Fallback names a specific, workable alternative. | Trigger condition quality: Trigger names a specific date or event tied to the deadline.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
